newsitem.title: GERMANY: CDU'S Geissler backs easier EMU terms, against delay.
newsitem.headline: CDU'S Geissler backs easier EMU terms, against delay.

text.p: Heiner Geissler, deputy floor leader in parliament for Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU), spoke out on Friday for a looser reading of the Maastricht criteria rather than a delay in launching Europe's monetary union (EMU).

Geissler, the highest-ranking Kohl ally to urge a shift from Bonn's strict interpretation of the treaty's three percent deficit-to-GDP target, said Germany had manoeuvered itself into a self-made trap with its "criteria fetishism" over the euro.
"I would consider it one of the worst mistakes possible to delay the euro because of the question of 3.0 percent or 3.2 percent," Geissler told German Radio.
"The Bundesbank president himself has said he did not invent the 3.0 target. So we have to get out of this self-made trap if we want to be able to function politically."

Kohl's centre-right coalition has been bubbling with talk about how to launch the euro since Finance Minister Theo Waigel failed to have the powerful Bundesbank central bank revalue its gold and pay him the profits to meet the 3.0 percent target.

On Thursday evening, Waigel denied a report that his Bavarian-based Christian Social Union (CSU) party was considering delaying the planned 1999 euro launch because of the Socialist victory in the French parliamentary election.

Geissler, a long-time colleague and sometime critic of Kohl, said Germany should raise taxes and increase its new borrowing moderately to overcome its current budget problems. Waigel has said he still needs 19 billion marks ($11 billion) to make ends meet in his 1997 budget.
